orbit.title: The radar dancing over Cochabamba
orbit.intro: NISAR circles the Earth every ~100 minutes and repeats the same orbit every 12 days. Its radar sees through clouds and at night, so it can track water, soil and terrain in our basins all year round.
orbit.disclaimerPosition: Position computed from public orbital elements (TLE) with the SGP4 model. This is not live telemetry.
orbit.disclaimerPass: A predicted orbital pass does not guarantee that NISAR acquires an image: that depends on its observation plan.
orbit.disclaimerSwath: The swath is illustrative: the real radar looks sideways, not straight down.
orbit.tleStale: Orbital elements are more than {{days}} days old: the position may be inaccurate.
orbit.error: Could not get the NISAR orbit
orbit.pendingCatalog: Will appear once the backend catalog is available.

typeWhy.crecida_torrencial: Fast and powerful: the stream rises in minutes and carries sediment.

how.title: We combine 4 clues from space and the ground

lluvia.title: Rain
lluvia.text: NASA satellites measure rain every 30 minutes.

suelo.title: Wet soil
suelo.text: If it rained in previous days, the ground can't absorb more.

terreno.title: Terrain
terreno.text: Relief tells where water and mud flow down.

radar.title: Radar
radar.text: NISAR sees through clouds whether water or mud appeared.

how.result: Every 30 minutes we compute a color per district and send it instantly.
how.formula:
núcleo = lluvia × (0,5 + 0,5 × terreno) — con suelo empapado los umbrales de lluvia bajan hasta 40 %
riesgo = 100 × (0,8 × núcleo + 0,2 × radar)
verde < 25 ≤ amarillo < 50 ≤ naranja < 75 ≤ rojo · sube al instante, baja tras 12 h
how.limits: Sources: GPM IMERG, Copernicus DEM 30 m, GAMC districts and gullies, NISAR / Sentinel-1. Limit: one rain pixel spans ~10 km.

eval.sub: Tested on {{n}} real days in Bolivia, with and without emergencies.
eval.improving: We still raise {{n}} false alarms on very rainy days without damage. The satellite measures 10 km squares and can't single out a storm over a small ravine: that needs ground rain gauges (SENAMHI) and the GAMC incident record.

rain.title: Rain measured from space
rain.source: NASA GPM IMERG · every 30 min · last 24 h
rain.total: Columns = total rain in 24 h (up to {{mm}} mm)
rain.howToRead: Each map column is a 10 × 10 km square measured by the satellite: taller and darker = more rain.
rain.preliminary: The latest hours are preliminary (about 4 h delay).
